title: Positive design: build the redesign as a rendered prototype, not a prose spec
description: Per council/socaity-0hb.md Amendment 1, process clause. The previous design was specified as prose, implemented by tickets each verified against its own checklist, and never looked at as a rendered whole until the founder did - at which point it was found to be an unapplied token layer over a default stylesheet. This ticket inverts that: the product-designer builds the positive design AS A WORKING RENDER through the real toolchain, iterating visually until it is good, and the artifact is what gets reviewed and decomposed. Scope: the masthead component (A3), the manifesto first screen and its 144px void, /roadmap as a designed surface (A7), the node page contest section and the collapsed provenance (A4, A6), /ledger's empty external-contributor row promoted out of 94% scroll depth and out of the dotted-means-inert idiom, and /claim's wrapping commands (A7). title: W4a card.html for every M0 surface, og tags, and the A1 disclosure split

Order is load-bearing: top strip, headline, then .card__register at >=44px IMMEDIATELY under the headline, then .card__detail at 32px, then footer strip. No webfont dependency; DESIGN AGAINST THE RESOLVED FALLBACK ON ALL THREE PLATFORMS, not against Charter - the 44px measurement must hold in the widest member of the stack. /faq card headline is THE CONSENT SENTENCE, not 'Frequently asked questions' - that makes the maintainer-trust asset the first thing a maintainer meets. title: W2a Status chips: no hue, new markers, legend as details
description: Per council/socaity-0hb.md Resolution (adopted by consent). DoD: tools/check.sh green (byte-identical) AND tools/gates/html_gate.py green. No check lands red. In style.css, confine your edits to your own named section header inside its @layer so the four W2 tickets merge cleanly. / Section D. Kill the pill: 2px radius, no fill, 1px --rule-strong border, --t-micro, 8px ::before marker. NO HUE ANYWHERE IN THE STATUS SYSTEM - render only in the ink family: --ink for live (open, contested), --ink-2 for resolved (confirmed, settled), --ink-3 for inert (withdrawn, reserved). Contested is therefore the DARKEST chip on the page, which reads as emphasis: contestation is the mechanism working, not a fault. Markers: open = hollow square, confirmed/settled = filled square, CONTESTED = SQUARE WITH A VERTICAL DIVIDER (reads as two sides; survives 8px), withdrawn = dotted outline, reserved = dashed outline. THE 45-DEGREE HATCH IS RESERVED EXCLUSIVELY FOR PROVENANCE (W2b) and must appear nowhere in the status vocabulary. --flag-contested/--flag-settled are reserved for genuine defects only (stale estimates, CI drift). Never twice for the same fact on one row (the ledger's duplicate 'confirmed' goes); never inside a heading. Legend collapses to <details> summarised 'what these marks mean', sitting BELOW the contest section in source order and forced open in @media print. The contest section carries the same visual weight as Requires and Competing approaches, sits adjacent to the claim it contests, and is NEVER inside a details. Microcopy: 'dispute' becomes 'read the contest'. Ships with html_gate check (c): .chip with no text node. WATCH-ITEM ON REVIEW: contested must never migrate to --ink-3.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text:
Resolution (platform-engineer, resolvable alone per charter):
DECIDED — M0/M1 run on a deliberately boring stack: one web app, one relational database, one signed append-only event log (files or a single log table). No runtime dependency on ComputeNet before M3.
Rationale: (1) milestones.md names the market window as the binding constraint; substrate work does not advance M1's done-criterion (a stranger uses the triage tool). Under those two rules, replaying the log into ComputeNet at M3/M4 is a data migration, not a rewrite.
Substrate hardening deadlines (from knowledge.md): M3 metered capacity, M4 live multi-writer graph, M5 replay-grade determinism. Revisit then.

title: Deferred redemption does not defer attack profitability: declare a ledger challenge/clawback policy at M0
description:
Context: vision.md 'Credit' defers fiat redemption 'until the defense layer has been battle-tested — the moment credit converts to money, every attack becomes profitable'. But the ledger is append-only from M0 and M5 promises retroactive distribution honoring entries all the way back to M0. So attacks on the ledger are profitable NOW: an adversary games entries during M0-M2 (before any verification market exists, per milestones.md M3) and collects at M5. Deferral moves the payout, not the attack window — it may even widen it, since the cheapest time to farm entries is precisely when defenses do not exist.
Question: What is the declared policy for challenging, discounting, or clawing back pre-M5 ledger entries before the first retroactive distribution executes — e.g. a mandatory ex-post audit of all entries by the M3 verification market, a challenge period, or correlated-identity discounting — and is it published at M0 as part of the standing commitment?
Why it matters: The red-flag rule: any metric that pays out before an adversary's attack cost is recovered is unsafe; here payout timing is M5 but entry timing is M0, so the entire pre-defense ledger is the attack surface. An unannounced clawback at M5 breaks the promise that recruited early contributors; an announced one at M0 is just part of the rule. This must be embedded in the distribution rule code (blocks that issue). Legal-counsel: clawback of promised distributions has contract-law implications.

Core: (1) entries born provisional, only confirmed entries pay; (2) mandatory pre-distribution audit of all pre-M3 entries by the M3 verification market, funded by a capped published slice of the pie; (3) public challenge window between provisional-pool announcement and binding declaration, challenged entries escrowed at declared weight, never redistributed; (4) correlated-identity discounting via algorithm published at M0, prospectively amendable only, cluster-level human review (GDPR art. 22); (5) confirmation fixes eligibility+relative weight, amounts arise only on declaration, non-transferable, platform never initiates recovery of settled distributions; (6) invariant: fabrication cost + evasion cost > expected payout; (7) enumerated challenge grounds, reputation-only stakes (bad-faith standard), notice + 30d response, verification-market adjudication, one staked appeal, pre-M3 challenges queue with no founder interim adjudication. Full deliberation: council/socaity-zjr.md. Scope note added to socaity-1ux: counsel review must cover this policy text; vocabulary is validation/challenge, never clawback.

description: Context: milestones.md M0 ('ledger has recorded its first external contribution', 'ledger always') and sustainability.md (founder labor on ledger from day zero). title: Publish the epoch-share distribution rule as code before the first external ledger entry

title: Ledger event schema v1: observations vs valuations, hash chain, versioning
description:
Context: vision.md 'Credit' + milestones.md Principle 3 say the append-only public ledger runs from day zero, and M5's retroactive distribution will replay events written years earlier. knowledge: schema is a wire protocol.
Question: Define ledger event schema v1: content-addressed hash-chained entries with explicit version field; strict separation of observation events (labor hours, PR merged, capacity metered — immutable) from valuation events (credit assigned — replayable with new parameters); fixed-point/rational arithmetic for all credit math; timestamps from events, never wall clock. What observation types must exist from entry #1 so M5 replay does not find gaps? Which observations does mechanism-designer's epoch-share math require (epoch boundaries, declared rates, capacity units)?
Why it matters: Blocks M0 done-criterion ('ledger has recorded its first external contribution'). Any observation not recorded from day zero can never be reconstructed; the standing retroactive commitment is only credible if a stranger can recompute balances from the log.

comments.text:
Platform-engineer proposal for council (needs mechanism-designer sign-off on the observation taxonomy):
Schema v1 skeleton: entry = {version, prev_hash, entry_hash, event_time, actor_key, kind, payload}. kinds split into observations (labor.recorded, pr.merged, capacity.metered, pledge.made, verification.performed, funds.received) and valuations (credit.assigned, epoch.closed, parameters.changed). Observations are immutable facts; valuations are derived and re-derivable — M5's retroactive distribution is a replay of observations under final parameters, so parameters.changed must itself be a ledger event.
Open for mechanism-designer: (a) minimal observation set epoch-share math needs from day zero — epoch boundary definition, declared founder rate, capacity unit; (b) whether declared rates are observations (I say yes: 'rate X was declared at T' is a fact even if the valuation it feeds is retuned).
Arithmetic: integer/rational only in anything credit-touching; floats forbidden.
Blocked by socaity-ef7 (PII split) and socaity-h20 (actor_key semantics) before v1 freezes.

title: Close the gap: how attribution.claimed gets the contributor's own signature
description:
Found while building socaity-4qy (/claim flow).

The ipg resolution's done-condition is 'the first attribution.claimed with actor lineage != founder keys' -- i.e. the first NON-FOUNDER SIGNATURE on the chain. The /claim page's three ssh-keygen blocks produce a bidirectional GitHub attestation (sshsig, namespace socaity.dev/claim), and tools/claim/verify_claim.py verifies it and derives actor_key (z6Mk), claim_binding and attestation_hash. That is everything the ledger needs EXCEPT the event signature itself.

The gap: ledger/validator.py requires sig = raw Ed25519 over the RFC 8785 canonical event bytes (sig_alg 'ed25519', ledger/crypto.py VERIFIERS). ssh-keygen -Y sign cannot produce that -- SSHSIG signs a wrapped blob (MAGIC||namespace||reserved||hash_alg||H(msg)), and there is no ssh-keygen path to a raw signature over arbitrary bytes. The contributor also cannot build the canonical event themselves without knowing prev (chain head) and ts.

So today nobody can actually append attribution.claimed as the contributor with ssh-keygen alone, and the /claim page deliberately does not claim otherwise -- it stops at 'publish the attestation' and says the entry then stops reading 'attribution reserved'.

Options to decide between (council question, probably ipg/7mk/zyt participants):
  (a) register an sshsig-aware verifier under a new sig_alg (e.g. 'ssh-ed25519') in ledger/crypto.VERIFIERS -- ~40 lines, stdlib only, already implemented as parsing code in tools/claim/verify_claim.py; but 7mk froze sig_alg semantics, so this is a schema-level decision, not an implementation choice;
  (b) ship a fourth command: a small signer that reads the OpenSSH private key and signs the canonical event (breaks the ipg three-block / <2min budget and the 'ssh-keygen only' toolchain);
  (c) rule that attribution.claimed may be maintainer-signed with the attestation hash as the binding -- which would mean M0's done-condition can be met with zero non-founder signatures, and MD's paramount in ipg Round 2 rules that out explicitly.

Blocking for M0's done-condition, not for the /claim page itself.

title: Define M0 success metrics and the inbound intake path
description: Context: milestones.md M0 done-when includes 'the ledger has recorded its first external contribution'; launch doctrine says the metric is aligned inbound, not traffic. socaity-e1g covers long-run cohort instrumentation; this is the narrow M0 definition. / Question: define 'aligned inbound' operationally and stand up the intake path before launch so day-one signal is not lost. / Why it matters: without a pre-agreed definition and a working intake path, M0 cannot be honestly declared done and the highest-value asset of the launch (the list of aligned people) evaporates in unlogged DMs.
close_reason: Resolved in comment: metrics defined (aligned inbound + external ledger entries, traffic explicitly excluded), intake path specified (canonical mailbox + start-here page + same-day logging).

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Resolution (launch-strategist, resolvable within role): (1) METRICS — M0 is judged on: (a) aligned inbound: count of unsolicited contacts that name a specific way they want to contribute (capacity, expertise, money, or amplification-with-standing); a 'love this, good luck' email does not count. Target: 20+ in the first two weeks, of which 5+ convert to a logged action. (b) First external ledger entries: count and diversity of contributors (2+ distinct externals beats 10 entries from one person). (c) Explicitly NOT metrics: HN points, traffic, stars — track them privately for channel calibration, never report them as success. (2) INTAKE PATH — one canonical email (hello@socaity.dev) plus a 'start here' page linked from the manifesto's last line listing 3-5 concrete first contributions (per socaity-ipg); every inbound gets logged same-day to a private CRM sheet with source, cohort guess, and named intent, so the aligned-inbound count is auditable against the definition above. No Discord/community channel is required for M0 intake (see socaity-vqo for that decision) — a single logged mailbox is enough at this scale and loses nothing. (3) The definition of 'aligned inbound' ships in the launch plan (socaity-bxo) so the founder is not tempted to redefine success after the fact.

description: Context: milestones.md M1 done-when: 'a stranger uses it on their own repo because it is the best triage tool available to them, network aside.' The agentic issue-triage space is crowded (GitHub Copilot-native triage, Linear/Height AI features, standalone agents). / Question: which tools does the target developer actually compare us to, what one-line differentiator survives that comparison (candidate: the only triage tool that outputs a dependency-aware AND/OR needs graph with explicit alternatives, not a ranked list), and does that line survive message-testing on real developers before M1 ships? / Why it matters: M1 recruits the graph-populators every later milestone needs (milestones.md recruitment chain); positioning that leads with the movement instead of the tool, or a tool claim that loses a side-by-side, starves the chain at its second link.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Partial analysis (launch-strategist): the comparison set a developer will actually invoke: GitHub-native AI triage (Copilot autofix/issue features), project-tracker AI (Linear triage, Height autonomous features), coding agents pointed at backlogs (Claude Code, Devin, OpenHands), and older dep-graph analytics (Libraries.io — relevant to M2, not M1). None of these produce a dependency-aware AND/OR decomposition with explicit alternative solution branches; all produce either ranked lists or direct patches. Candidate line to test: 'Point it at your repo and get a dependency-aware map of what your backlog actually is — which issues are the same issue, which block which, and what the alternatives are — not another ranked list.' Two risks the test must probe: (a) 'AND/OR graph' is vocabulary developers do not have — the demo has to show it, the copy must not say it; (b) the honest gap: if decomposition quality is mediocre (see socaity-q8b eval harness), no positioning survives contact. Remaining open: message-test on 5+ real developers outside the warm circle; needs product-designer for how the graph demo carries the claim.

title: Specify the foundationalness measure formally and run a Goodhart analysis before M2 publishes it
description:
Context: vision.md 'Pricing the commons' defines the subsidy signal only 'roughly' — downstream unlocked value relative to direct demand, 'a centrality measure'. milestones.md M2 computes and publishes this index on real ecosystem data as the flagship traction artifact.
Question: Which measure exactly? Betweenness and eigenvector centrality are both manipulable by edge insertion; PageRank-family measures have known link-farm attacks; the OR-node probabilistic flow needs a defined semantics. Required: (a) a formal definition including OR-branch weighting and decay, (b) a Goodhart pass per taxonomy class — regressional (noise in value estimates), extremal (adversarially-grown graphs vs organic ones), causal (edge fabrication, need-splitting), adversarial (coordinated modeling of the metric), (c) sensitivity analysis on real M2 data: how much does one fabricated dependency edge move a node's rank?
Why it matters: M2's index is computed on data adversaries do not yet control, but publishing the metric publishes the attack target for M4, when the same measure prices credit. Choosing a measure whose gaming cost is known and priced (contesting an edge must be cheaper than fabricating one — price the asymmetry explicitly) is far cheaper before the index is cited and ossified. Data-analyst owns the M2 computation; platform-engineer's deterministic simulation is the lab for the adversarial-growth experiments.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Scope fixed by socaity-155 resolution: formalize F(v) = Σ d(s)·R(s,v) (reliability semantics, damping, gap function g) and run the Goodhart pass on the demand-source validation gate + equivalence-class machinery. The operator choice is settled — do not reopen; the spec and attack analysis remain.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Re-scoped to execution by the socaity-155 resolution: the operator is decided (F(v) = Σ d(s)·R(s,v), reliability semantics, gap function g, validation gate). Remaining work = write the formal spec document and run the Goodhart pass on the demand-source gate + equivalence-class machinery (attack catalog per the MD knowledge layer). title: Funder sequencing strategy for the M0-M2 bridge
description: Context: sustainability.md §5 lists NLnet, STF, Prototype Fund, RetroPGF, Gitcoin as the bridge funders; knowledge.md holds the funder profiles. / Question: In what order, with what role for each funder, should the bridge pipeline run? / Why it matters: a mediocre-fit application costs a month and a reputation (SKILL.md); the sequence determines when money can realistically arrive relative to founder runway.
close_reason: Sequencing settled from role expertise; recorded in comment. Execution items tracked in socaity-bg4/4we/8nz/ryv.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text:
Resolution (grant-writer expertise, knowledge.md funder profiles + pipeline discipline):

1. NLnet/NGI Zero — primary and only grantee-track target for the bridge. Two focused asks: M1 graph tool at the next call, M2 observatory the call after (socaity-4we, socaity-8nz). Rationale: EUR 5k-50k, ~2-page applications, technologist reviewers, milestone-MoU payment, NL founder + open-source + commons framing is the strongest natural fit available. On rejection: request feedback, revise, resubmit next call — NLnet explicitly welcomes this.
2. Sovereign Tech Agency — NOT a grant target during the bridge (socaity is too new; STA funds maintenance of existing critical infrastructure). Approach instead as the M2 observatory's first customer/data-partner once an index prototype exists: their portfolio-selection problem is what the index computes, and their funding choices become citable validation ('STA funded N of our top 20').
3. Prototype Fund — deprioritized pending verification (socaity-bg4): pre-restructuring rules required German residency, likely excluding an NL founder. No writing time unless verification shows changed rules.
4. EU NGI successors / Horizon cascade calls — opportunistic second priority; more paperwork per euro than NLnet. Watch, don't chase.
5. Optimism RetroPGF / Gitcoin — from M2 at the earliest (retro rounds reward shipped impact) and only after the public no-token rationale exists (socaity-ryv).
6. Foundations (Sloan/Ford/Omidyar/Mozilla/OTF) — cultivation starts at M2 using the index + press as door-opener; expect money M3+, not bridge money.

Discipline: one core narrative (xz/log4j concreteness -> computable Pigouvian subsidy -> observatory as proof), adapted per funder; decline mediocre-fit calls — they cost a month and a reputation.

title: Technique for forcing competing OR branches (anti-solution-bias) in the decomposer
description: Context: vision.md 'The needs graph': modeling alternatives explicitly prevents the first decomposition from ossifying; knowledge.md names solution bias the top decomposition failure mode. / Question: What concrete generation technique makes the M1 decomposer reliably produce genuinely competing OR branches rather than one approach plus strawmen? / Why it matters: OR-branch quality drives probabilistic value flow — foundationalness scores are only as good as the alternatives modeled, so a solution-biased decomposer silently corrupts the Pigouvian signal.
close_reason: Resolved in comment: multi-call independent branch generation with problem-restatement gate, null branch, and distinctness filter.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Resolution (agent-engineer, resolvable alone): use a three-stage pipeline rather than one-shot decomposition. (1) Problem restatement first: the model must restate the need with zero solution vocabulary before any branching — reject restatements containing implementation nouns. (2) Parallel independent branch generation: sample K solution approaches in separate calls with distinct persona/constraint prompts (e.g. minimal-dependency approach, buy-not-build approach, do-nothing/workaround approach), never in one call — single-call 'list 3 alternatives' reliably yields one real option plus strawmen. Always include the null branch (workaround/no-build) so foundationalness is priced against a real baseline. (3) Adversarial distinctness filter: an LLM judge scores pairwise branch distinctness on mechanism, not phrasing; merge branches that differ only in wording, and require at least 2 surviving branches or flag the node 'alternatives unexplored' rather than faking an OR. Eval hook for socaity-q8b: rubric measures whether a known-shipped alternative from the golden project appears among generated branches (recall over historical alternatives).

Nothing specifies how an index entry (a repo/package with foundationalness and support scores) is represented in the needs graph so an agent and the ledger can target it. / Question: define the mapping — is an under-supported project a problem node, a standing maintenance node (vision.md 'Maintenance is continuous credited work'), or an external leaf — and which fields (scores, evidence dossier, dependency edges) carry over with what provenance? / Why it matters: this is the seam where the traction hack (M2) joins the product (M1/M3); if the schemas diverge, M3's contribution loop needs a manual re-entry step and the dogfooding story breaks.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] RESOLUTION (adopted by consent, round 2; covers 3jq): Two stores, one-way seam — index = versioned recomputable snapshot dataset; platform nodes materialize only on trigger (user citation / 3o2 consent / curator spotlight) with ingested_from pinning and pipeline-on_behalf_of provenance; computed numbers render by snapshot reference, never stored on nodes; observations re-crawled, claims contested. Agent-actionable = two axes never a scalar: receptivity GATES (hard 3o2 consent tiers — consent structurally impossible to outweigh; not-yet-asked renders as outreach candidate never target) and specifiability RANKS (executed-build gate + tests + license + tracker; non-summed facets with documented gaming vectors) doubling as the t46 context-pack feasibility vector; calibration loop logs targeting outcomes from day one. Full deliberation: council/socaity-15b.md

title: M1 graph schema must capture mechanism-critical provenance or later defenses cannot be retrofitted
description:
Context: vision.md 'The needs graph' makes edges contestable claims and prices commons via centrality; the threat-model defenses (contestable edges, correlated-identity discounting, OR-node probabilistic flow) all consume provenance data. milestones.md M1 builds the graph tool single-player, where it is tempting to skip provenance because there is no adversary yet.
Question: Which fields are mandatory on every node and edge from M1 day one so that M2-M4 mechanisms can be computed retroactively: asserter identity (human vs agent, and which agent), assertion timestamp, evidence links, contest/dispute history, OR-branch probability estimates with estimator provenance, and node-type (for per-type decay half-lives)? Decide the minimal set now.
Why it matters: The subsidy signal and every Goodhart defense are functions of WHO asserted WHAT WHEN. If M1 graphs (including ingested GitHub issue trackers) lack provenance, the earliest and most-cited graphs become permanently unpriceable or must be discarded at M4 — and agent-generated nodes indistinguishable from human demand would silently corrupt the person-weighted demand principle (vision.md 'The demand side') from the first day. Schema is cheap now, impossible later. Agent-engineer: decomposition agents must stamp their outputs; platform-engineer: schema lives in the ComputeNet-backed data model.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Satisfied by socaity-sbb resolution: mandatory provenance block (actor_kind, on_behalf_of, model, prompt_hash, run_id, evidence hashes) on every node/edge/estimate from M0, CI-enforced. See council/socaity-sbb.md

comments.author: MacBoo

description: Context: knowledge.md checklist: 'everything open-licensed (AGPL/Apache/CC — have the answer ready; NLnet requires open outcomes).' vision.md Principles require open source + forkable data but name no license. / Question: Which license for platform code (AGPL to protect forkability vs Apache for adoption), which for graph and ledger data (ODbL/CC-BY?), which for the M2 index dataset — and does the choice keep the observatory service model (sustainability.md §3: 'data forkable; freshness, curation, accountability are not') coherent? / Why it matters: NLnet applications must state licenses; changing later is expensive; the license is also the technical form of the forkability guarantee the vision treats as its capture-check.

title: M0 roadmap-as-graph: storage format and conventions
description:
Context: milestones.md M0: 'socaity.dev's own roadmap becomes the first needs graph, expressed in its own conventions (AND/OR nodes, contestable edges)'.
Question: What concrete artifact is the M0 roadmap-graph? Proposal: declarative files in the public repo (one file per node, YAML/JSON; problem|solution type; OR-children on problems, AND-children on solutions; edges as explicit assertion records), conforming to the M1 graph identity model so M1 ingests it without migration. Beads issues can be referenced but the graph format is the source of truth for graph semantics.
Why it matters: M0's done-criterion requires the roadmap-as-graph to be public; doing it in a throwaway format creates a migration debt at M1 and undercuts the dogfooding claim.

title: Model the earliness premium curve: bound the early-vs-late claim ratio before promising it
description:
Context: vision.md 'Credit' — epoch-share pricing gives early contributors 'a bigger claim on the future'; milestones.md M5 honors shares back to M0. With a fixed pie per epoch and a network growing orders of magnitude, the ratio between an M0 hour and an M4 hour of identical work is unbounded a priori and is determined entirely by epoch length and pie schedule.
Question: Model claim-share trajectories under plausible growth scenarios: for candidate pie schedules (constant, geometric decay, contribution-indexed growth), what is the resulting M0:M4 claim ratio per unit of contribution, and what ratio range is (a) sufficient to compensate early risk, (b) defensible publicly, (c) not so extreme that late contributors rationally stay out (the reverse-bootstrap failure)?
Why it matters: The earliness premium is the M0 recruitment instrument AND a future optics/regulatory liability if the curve is too steep (looks like founder/insider enrichment — see Bitcoin early-miner and airdrop-insider discourse). The pie schedule must be fixed inside the distribution-rule code, so this analysis blocks that decision. First pass is analytic; strategic-agent simulation on ComputeNet can wait.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Scope sharpened by socaity-x8o resolution: model epoch length L and the P_e curve; constant P_e is the default recommendation (growing denominator IS the premium); only a decaying schedule is admissible as an alternative — no premium multiplier. Values fix before M0 publication via the meta-rule.

title: Graph identity model: stable node IDs, edge lifecycle, merge-as-redirect — before M1 writes real data
description:
Context: vision.md 'The needs graph' (contestable edges; merge/split as first-class contestable operations; nodes age) and M1 (strangers populate real graphs) / M4 (merge-split as credited work).
Question: Fix the graph data model before M1 persists real user data: (a) stable, globally unique node IDs that survive merges (merge = redirect, never delete; edits follow redirects — Wikidata precedent); (b) edges as first-class entities with status asserted/disputed/settled, never deleted; (c) every assertion carries provenance (human, agent, GitHub-ingestion) and timestamp so re-ingestion is idempotent and value-decay is computable. What graph write operations does the M1 agent decomposition loop actually need?
Why it matters: M1's schema is the substrate M4's contestation and merge/split must run on; retrofitting redirects and edge status onto a naively-mutable M1 schema means migrating strangers' live data. Cheap now, expensive forever after.

title: Append-only public ledger vs GDPR erasure: keep PII off the log
description:
Context: vision.md 'Radical transparency' + 'needs are sensitive'; the ledger is append-only and public from day zero (milestones.md Principle 3); founder labor recorded publicly (sustainability.md backbone).
Question: The ledger will contain personal data (contributor identifiers, work descriptions) that GDPR erasure rights may later demand we delete — but the log is immutable and mirrored. Proposed architecture: log stores only pseudonymous keys and content hashes; any PII (display names, free-text descriptions) lives in an off-log mutable store referenced by hash, so erasure removes the referent while the chain stays intact. Is that sufficient under EU law, and what does it imply for 'entries a stranger can recompute balances from'?
Why it matters: An erasure demand against an immutable mirrored log is unresolvable after the fact; the split must be designed into schema v1 (blocks the ledger schema decision).

title: Portable contributor identity for ledger attribution from entry #1

Question: How are contributors identified in ledger entries from M0 onward? Proposal: entries attribute to a user-held public key (contributor signs their own contribution events where feasible); platform accounts map to keys, never replace them. What key scheme, custody UX, and recovery story clears the bar for the first handful of M0 contributors without heavyweight ceremony?
Why it matters: Retroactive distribution at M5 pays whoever the ledger names; if names are platform-issued rows, a fork cannot honor them and the earliness-premium promise silently becomes platform-locked. This must be right in the first entries, not retrofitted.

description:

title: Compute credit: non-transferability between users as a standing design constraint (MiCA/e-money cliff edge)
description: Context: vision.md 'Credit' layer 2 — compute credit is closed-loop, wage-like, redeemable only in network agent-hours; fiat on-ramp before off-ramp. Question: Record as a binding constraint that compute credit is (a) not transferable between users and (b) not redeemable for fiat, until a specific legal review gates any change. Closed-loop instruments redeemable only in services on the issuing platform generally fall outside EMD2 e-money (claim accepted by third parties) — but user-to-user transferability plus any secondary market makes it a de facto exchange token and drags it into MiCA territory regardless of the no-token position. The fiat off-ramp (M5) re-opens redeemability analysis the moment it is considered. Why it matters: The 'no token issuance' anti-commitment (sustainability.md) is necessary but not sufficient; transferability is the actual cliff edge. Mechanism-designer needs this constraint before designing credit flows, pledge mechanics, or planner economics that might assume credits can move between participants.

title: Append-only public ledger vs GDPR: personal data in ledger entries and the right to erasure
description: Context: milestones.md principle 3 — the contribution ledger is append-only and public from day zero (M0 'done when' includes the first external contribution recorded). vision.md demand-side allows pseudonymity but the ledger records contributors. Question: What personal data do ledger entries carry (names/handles, declared rates, timestamps)? An immutable public record containing personal data collides with GDPR art. 17 erasure and art. 16 rectification. Design options: ledger stores only pseudonymous contributor keys with the key-to-identity mapping held off-ledger and severable; tombstone/redaction conventions that preserve append-only hash integrity while removing personal data. Why it matters: Material before M0/M1 — the first entries written at M0 set the schema; retrofitting pseudonymization onto a published append-only ledger is exactly the failure mode GDPR-by-design exists to prevent. Related: ledger event schema v1 issue (socaity-zyt).

Does any planned mechanism feature (pledge vesting, compute-credit interaction, M5 retroactive distribution) violate these? Why it matters: These four properties are what keeps epoch shares out of securities/participation-right territory under NL/EU law. If mechanism design ever needs to relax one, that is a stop-and-get-counsel moment, not a tuning decision. Feeds the M0 wording decision.

title: Pricing heterogeneous M0-M2 contributions with no market: valuation rule and the founder rate-setting conflict
description:
Context: sustainability.md 'The backbone' records founder labor 'at a publicly declared rate', and M0-M2 contributions (manifesto edits, design docs, code, outreach) hit the ledger before any market or verification mechanism exists to price them. The founder both sets the rate schedule and is the largest epoch-share beneficiary — the exact 'founder-tuned parameters that move founder income' conflict sustainability.md itself names.
Question: (a) What is the valuation rule for heterogeneous pre-market contributions — a published rate card per contribution class, time-based at declared rates, or negotiated-per-entry with public reasoning? (b) What commitment device constrains the founder as price-setter — rate changes apply only prospectively, a cap on founder share per epoch, or third-party attestation of rates?
Why it matters: Regressional Goodhart — credit for estimated value pays estimation error, and at M0 the estimator is the conflicted party. The manifesto's credibility with exactly the M0 cohort (people who read incentive designs critically) depends on this being visibly solved, not waved at. Community-builder: this is a trust asset or liability at recruitment time.

title: Support-axis false negatives: corporate-employed maintainers read as unfunded
description: Context: milestones.md M2 uses GitHub Sponsors / Open Collective / OpenSSF criticality as funding signals. A package with zero sponsorship whose maintainer is paid by Google to maintain it is not under-supported; sponsorship data is sparse and skewed. / Question: what is the concrete methodology for detecting corporate-backed maintenance (commit email domains, org membership, employer declarations) and how does the index represent conflicting or absent signals? / Why it matters: publicly listing a well-staffed project as 'least-supported' is the single most likely way the M2 index gets dunked on at its press moment; M2's 'done when: cited by people we did not contact' depends on credibility surviving first contact.
close_reason: Methodology decided: affiliation detection + ternary support with 'unknown' never published as zero + per-entry evidence dossiers; pre-contact as final check. Recorded in comments.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Resolution (data-analyst, resolvable alone): three-part methodology. (1) Detection: for each project's top committers/reviewers/release authors over trailing 12 months, infer corporate affiliation from commit email domains, GitHub org membership, and public employer fields; classify maintenance capacity as corporate-backed when a majority of maintenance activity comes from affiliated accounts (include bot-account attribution to their operating org). (2) Representation: the support axis is ternary at the evidence level — 'supported', 'under-supported', 'unknown'. When funding signals are absent but affiliation signals conflict or are undetectable, support is UNKNOWN, never zero; 'unknown' entries are excluded from the published least-supported top-N and listed separately as 'insufficient evidence'. (3) Presentation: every published entry ships an evidence dossier (funding links checked, affiliation checks run, dates) so a wrong entry is a correctable data error, not a methodology scandal. Residual risk (invisible employment, e.g. contractor arrangements) goes in the published limitations section, and the maintainer pre-contact pass (socaity-bza) is the final human check — pre-contact exists precisely to catch what detection misses.

title: Node identity and canonicalization across decomposer runs
description: Context: vision.md makes merging duplicates and connecting subgraphs first-class contestable operations; knowledge.md notes an unstable decomposer cannot be trusted to merge duplicate needs. / Question: How do nodes get stable identity when LLM decomposition is nondeterministic — same need, different runs, different phrasings? Options: content-addressed hashing (too brittle), embedding-similarity dedup with thresholds, decomposer-as-proposer with confirmed merges. / Why it matters: Without stable identity, re-running decomposition on an updated repo duplicates the whole graph, estimates and ledger references dangle, and M1's 'ingest the issue tracker' is not idempotent.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Recommendation (agent-engineer): treat the decomposer as a proposer, never an authority on identity. Nodes get random stable IDs at creation; identity is never derived from content (content-addressing breaks on the first rewording). Idempotent re-ingestion works by match-then-propose: embed each candidate node, retrieve nearest existing nodes, and above a high similarity threshold update-in-place, in a middle band emit a proposed-equivalence edge (a contestable claim per vision.md, confirmed by the user in M1 single-player mode), below it create new. This makes merge a first-class credited operation later, exactly as the vision wants, and keeps ledger/estimate references stable. Threshold values and the embedding model are empirical — feed into the socaity-q8b eval harness (measure duplicate rate and false-merge rate on repeated ingestion of the same repo). Leaving open until socaity-sbb fixes where IDs and equivalence edges live in the schema.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Partially resolved by socaity-sbb: permanent random IDs + match-then-propose confirmed as schema-level policy. Remaining open: empirical similarity thresholds — feed the socaity-q8b eval harness.

title: Index identity: package-level vs project-level, decided before any metric is computed
description: Context: milestones.md M2 ingests npm/PyPI/Maven/GitHub; monorepos (babel, aws-sdk) publish hundreds of packages from one repo, and naive package-level ranking multiplies one project's weight by its package count. / Question: is the unit of the M2 index the package or the project (repo), and how are package-level dependency edges rolled up to project identity? / Why it matters: every downstream number changes with this choice; deciding it after computation means recomputing everything, and getting it wrong is a classic way published rankings get embarrassed (vision.md 'Pricing the commons' credibility depends on the index surviving its press moment).
close_reason: Decided: project-level identity, package-level ingestion, auditable rollup. Recorded in comments.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Resolution (data-analyst, resolvable alone): the unit of the index is the PROJECT (source repo), with ingestion at package level. Rationale: (1) support signals (Sponsors, Open Collective, corporate employment) attach to repos/maintainers, not packages, so a package-level index cannot place anything on the support axis honestly; (2) project-level rollup neutralizes monorepo distortion (babel/aws-sdk); (3) actionability is repo-shaped — you point an agent at a repo. Method: compute dependency edges package-to-package, map packages to source repos (deps.dev and ecosyste.ms both carry this mapping), collapse intra-repo edges, dedupe reverse-dependency trees at project level before damping. Packages with no resolvable source repo are kept but flagged 'unmapped' and excluded from the published top-N (an unverifiable entry is an indefensible entry). Publish the package-to-project mapping table with the data release so the rollup is auditable and contestable.

title: M2 press strategy: embargoed pre-brief, the xz backtest as the story, and the fast-follow plan
description: Context: milestones.md M2 — the index is 'inherently press-worthy'; done-when is citation by people we did not contact. This is a data-journalism story, not a product launch. Depends on socaity-dad (backtest) and socaity-4ur (maintainer consent/outreach). / Question: build the press package (top-20 list as artifact, xz/log4j backtest headline, per-item evidence dossiers, methodology, one or two quotable maintainers via community-builder), the embargoed pre-brief list of OSS-sustainability-beat journalists and newsletter authors (exclusives on angles, never on data — data public day one), no-conference-week timing, and the standing fast-follow plan for the next xz-style incident, which is when the index actually enters the canon. / Why it matters: M2 is the traction hack and the platform's first fiat source (sustainability.md); uncoordinated publication wastes the only inherently newsworthy asset before M3.

title: Accessibility floor for the graph surfaces, specified before the first frontend commit
description: Context: SKILL.md — accessibility as principle, not polish; the constituency explicitly includes under-resourced users. Focus+context makes keyboard navigation tractable where canvases make it impossible. / Question: adopt as spec: full keyboard navigation of the graph, WCAG AA contrast, screen-reader structure that exposes the graph as lists and relationships (its true underlying shape), no information conveyed by color alone (probability weights included). / Why it matters: retrofitting accessibility onto a canvas is a rewrite; committing to focus+context makes it nearly free if specified before code exists.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Resolution (product-designer, adopted as spec): (1) Keyboard: every graph operation reachable without pointer — focus node is a roving tabindex; arrow keys move parent/child/sibling; enter drills, escape backs out via breadcrumb. (2) Semantics: the graph is exposed to assistive tech as nested lists and labeled relationships ('requires', 'alternative to'), never as an ARIA-role canvas; the focus+context view is literally a document outline, so screen-reader order equals visual order. (3) WCAG AA contrast on all text and UI chrome, including status chips and probability bars. (4) No meaning by color alone: OR-branch weights get a numeric label plus bar length; dispute status gets an icon plus text. (5) Test hook: the five-user M1 prototype test (socaity-8wg) includes one keyboard-only pass. This closes as specified; enforcement lands in frontend review checklists once code exists.

title: OR-branch probabilities: declared vs market-based weights, and pricing losing-branch information
description:
Context: vision.md 'The needs graph' — value flows through OR nodes probabilistically; 'a foundation is only as foundational as the likelihood that its branch wins'. vision.md 'Open questions' already flags losing-branch information pricing. The branch probabilities are themselves estimates that can be pumped (causal Goodhart): inflating your branch's probability inflates every node beneath it.
Question: (a) Should branch weights be declared (by asserters/agents), aggregated from demand, or market-based (prediction-market style, where being wrong costs the estimator)? (b) How is exploration of a losing branch credited — a fixed information bounty, retroactive share of the winning branch's value, or nothing? (c) What must M1 agents record when they estimate branches so any of these designs remains possible?
Why it matters: OR-node flow is a multiplier on the entire subsidy signal; a pumpable branch weight is a lever on every downstream node's price. Part (c) is early-binding via the M1 schema issue; parts (a)-(b) can be settled by M4 but need the design space held open. Agent-engineer: decomposition agents are the main initial estimators.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Display-side constraints fixed by socaity-6kb: whatever weight mechanism 36f designs, market-derived weights must render in a visually discontinuous channel from agent-guessed buckets, and bucket thresholds are frozen before weights carry economic consequence.

title: What earns a ledger entry pre-M3: minimum contribution unit and the interim acceptance oracle
description:
Context: milestones.md M0-M2 run the ledger with no verification market (that arrives at M3). vision.md threat model rejects self-declared capacity ('egalitarian standing derives from observable tenure and consistency'), but at M0 even tenure is farmable by low-effort presence, and cheap-talk contributions (comments, praise, drive-by suggestions) could accrue entries.
Question: (a) What is the minimum verifiable contribution unit that earns a ledger entry pre-M3? (b) Who is the acceptance oracle before the verification market exists, and is that role publicly declared?
Why it matters: Every pre-M3 entry is a claim on the M5 retroactive distribution; admitting unverifiable entries now creates the audit debt the clawback-policy issue must later clean up. Cheap to solve correctly at M0, expensive to litigate at M5.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text:
Resolution (mechanism-designer, resolvable from role expertise alone):

1. Minimum contribution unit: a ledger entry requires a merged, hash-addressable artifact — a commit, document, design, or recorded decision — attached to a specific graph node. No entries for unmerged work, comments, or presence. Cheap talk earns nothing; this is the anti-farming line and it costs us nothing at M0 because real M0 contributions (code, docs, designs) all clear it.

2. Interim acceptance oracle: pre-M3, the maintainer of the target repository accepts entries — i.e. the founder for socaity/ComputeNet repos. This is a centralized oracle and that is acceptable IF publicly declared: state in the ledger README that founder acceptance is the interim mechanism, replaced by the M3 verification market.

3. Auditability requirement: every entry records (artifact hash, node id, accepter identity, claimed units, rate applied). This makes every pre-M3 entry re-verifiable by the M3 market before the M5 distribution — which is exactly the input the clawback-policy decision (socaity-zjr) needs.

4. Tenure/consistency standing (vision.md threat model, capacity-fraction row) is computed only over accepted entries, never over self-declared activity.

Residual risk accepted: founder self-acceptance of founder entries is a conflict, but it is the same conflict as socaity-19p (rate-setting) and is mitigated by the same devices decided there. Closing; the conflict lives on in socaity-19p.

title: Grant-to-ledger mechanics before the fiat rail exists: how does M0-M2 grant money attach to nodes?
description: Context: sustainability.md §5: 'grants are recorded on the ledger like any other inflow — attached to nodes, distributed per contribution... the mechanism's first fiat.' But milestones.md M5 says fiat settlement and retroactive distribution happen last, after the defense layer is battle-tested. / Question: When a 2026 NLnet tranche arrives, what concretely happens? Options: (a) grant pays founder directly and the ledger merely records it as an inflow against the funded nodes (informational, no settlement); (b) some escrow-like accounting is prototyped early; (c) grants are explicitly exempted from settlement until M5 but counted in the retroactive base. Also: do grant-funded hours still accrue epoch shares, or is that double-counting? / Why it matters: the answer goes into every application's sustainability section and into the funder's audit trail; getting it wrong either breaks the standing retroactive commitment (trust asset) or accidentally makes the platform a money handler years early (regulatory exposure).

title: Observatory operating cost and freshness cadence — avoiding the Libraries.io fate
description: Context: sustainability.md #3 sells exactly what a fork cannot replicate: freshness, curation, accountability. Libraries.io proved the data is collectable and then went dormant; continuous multi-ecosystem ingestion has real compute/storage/API-quota costs. / Question: estimate the steady-state cost of the M2 pipeline at weekly vs monthly refresh, which sources rate-limit or charge at that cadence, and what the grant budget line should be (NLnet/STF applications need concrete figures, and lead times are months per sustainability.md sequencing). / Why it matters: an observatory that goes stale is worse than none — staleness is the exact failure mode of the prior art we position against, and the freshness promise is the revenue model.

title: Instrument milestone 'done when' criteria from day zero
description: Context: milestones.md defines done-when tests that are all measurements — M0 'ledger has recorded its first external contribution', M1 'a stranger uses it on their own repo', M2 'cited by people we did not contact'. None has an agreed measurement method; M2's requires citation/backlink tracking that must be running before launch to distinguish contacted from organic citers. / Question: for each of M0-M2, what is the operational metric, the data source (ledger events, tool telemetry consistent with radical transparency, media monitoring), and who reviews it? / Why it matters: the milestones gate each other; without instrumentation, 'done' becomes vibes, and the M2 criterion is literally unmeasurable retroactively.

title: M4 personhood-lite architecture: attestation menu issuing one migration-friendly credential
description: Context: milestones.md M4 'personhood-lite identity'; vision.md open questions ('which mechanism clears the bar without excluding the people the platform most needs'); SKILL charter: M4 threat is casual vote-stuffing, M5 is professional Sybil farms — do not let M4 choices foreclose M5 upgrades. / Question: Adopt the staged architecture: a menu of attestations (phone, eID, social vouching), each yielding the same anonymous 'one distinct human' credential (nullifier-based, per-context, unlinkable), with attestation *level* recorded so M5 can require harder attestations for money-touching actions without reissuing identities. Every mechanism must pass the exclusion audit (no smartphone / no gov ID / no bank / not EU / disability / at-risk pseudonymity) with a documented fallback path. / Why it matters: Fixes the credential *shape* early so M1-M3 account plumbing (keypairs, per-context identifiers) is compatible; defers the mechanism *choice* to M4 when the threat is real. Prevents both over-building at M4 and a breaking identity migration at M5.
close_reason: Architecture decided and recorded in comment; concrete mechanism choice deferred to M4 planning

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: RESOLVED (identity-specialist, solo — squarely within charter 'choosing and staging the personhood mechanism'). Decision: adopt the staged attestation-menu architecture. (1) Personhood is separated from identity: the platform only ever learns 'distinct human, counted once', never who. (2) At M4, a menu of attestation paths — phone verification, government eID where available, social vouching — each issues the SAME anonymous personhood credential (BBS+/Semaphore-style: one nullifier per human per context, unlinkable across contexts; per-context nullifiers also keep health wishes unlinkable from finance wishes). Menu design minimizes exclusion: no single gate. (3) The credential records its attestation LEVEL (weak/medium/strong). M4 demand voting accepts any level; M5 money-touching actions require strong attestation — users upgrade by adding an attestation to their existing credential, never by reissuing identity. This is the migration path that keeps M4 from foreclosing M5. (4) Standing exclusion audit applies to every attestation path: no smartphone / no gov ID / no bank / non-EU / disability (no biometric-only, no synchronous-ceremony-only paths) / at-risk pseudonymity — each 'excluded' answer requires a documented alternative path before the mechanism ships. (5) Explicitly rejected: iris biometrics (custody + crypto-brand risk contradicts no-token positioning, vision.md 'Prior art'), public-video PoH (privacy), contribution-history as a demand-side gate (resource-weighted by construction, violates vision.md 'The demand side'). What M0/M1 must do NOW: nothing beyond socaity-7mk's keypair primitive and socaity-8j4's substrate boundary — both are compatible with this shape by design. Concrete M4 mechanism choice (which attestations at launch, Sybil-cost targets) deferred to M4 planning with mechanism-designer, informed by socaity-3la and socaity-q6g.

title: Epoch shares create Sybil incentive on the supply ledger before M4 — name the identity assumption
description: Context: vision.md Credit (epoch-share earliness premium; 'egalitarian standing derives from observable tenure and consistency') and threat model row 'capacity-fraction gaming'. Personhood arrives only at M4, but the ledger promises retroactive money from M0 — so identity attacks pay before any personhood mechanism exists. / Question: For M0–M3, which ledger quantities are strictly resource-weighted (metered capacity — Sybil-neutral, splitting identities gains nothing) and which are per-identity (tenure, consistency, reputation, any per-identity bonus or epoch floor — Sybil-positive)? Model with mechanism-designer whether one human running N contributor keys ever earns more than the same human with one key. / Why it matters: If any pre-M4 reward term is per-identity rather than per-unit-capacity, the day-one ledger accumulates fake-identity claims that M5 must honor retroactively. The fix is a design rule now (nothing per-identity pays before personhood), not a mechanism later.

title: GDPR: DPIA before M4 and special-category demand data architecture (content severed from identity)
description: Context: vision.md demand side — needs are sensitive (health, finance, family); demand expression may be pseudonymous; M4 switches on person-weighted demand at scale. Question: (1) A DPIA is required before M4 (large-scale processing, potentially special-category data) — schedule it as an M4 entry gate. (2) Architecture constraint to record now: demand content stored severed from any identity linkage, with the linkage user-held — pseudonymous health/finance/family needs can still be special-category data under GDPR art. 9 if linkable. (3) Proof-of-personhood verification data (M4 personhood-lite) is itself high-risk processing — identity-specialist's mechanism choice determines the GDPR bill. Why it matters: Material before M4; the severed-linkage constraint must reach platform-engineer's data model long before M4 to avoid a rebuild.

title: Tax treatment of ledger accruals and deemed-employment exposure for regular contributors
description: Context: sustainability.md backbone — founder labor accrues on the ledger at a declared rate from day zero; distributions happen at M5. milestones.md M3+ has regular external contributors compensated in epoch shares. Question: (1) NL tax timing: are ledger accruals income when recorded or when distributed? Working analysis: discretionary-until-declared claims (per socaity-h2c constraints) are not taxable income until distribution declared — but the founder should get a one-off ruling/adviser confirmation before M5, and cross-border contributors are told plainly it is their local problem while the platform issues statements (socaity's DAC7/statements issue). (2) Wet DBA / deemed employment: contributors are self-directed (choose own nodes, own tooling, no instruction authority) — genuinely protective facts; the danger factor to avoid is any platform feature that starts directing work (the vision's 'never assigns work' principle is legally protective, keep it). Why it matters: Material before M3/M5; monitor wet DBA enforcement practice. Licensed tax adviser required before the first retroactive distribution.

title: DAC7 assessment and annual contributor statements: design the ledger to emit them from day one
description: Context: sustainability.md — grants and later fiat settle to contributors per the ledger; knowledge layer flags DAC7 (EU platform-operator reporting on payments to sellers/service-providers) as applying well before M5 feels big. Question: (1) At what point do socaity's settlements to contributors trigger DAC7 reporting duties for the platform operator, and what data must be collected (name, TIN, address) that the pseudonymity design must accommodate? (2) Task: ledger schema and tooling should be able to emit per-contributor annual statements (amounts credited, distributed, dates) from day one — the ledger makes this nearly free; retrofitting is expensive. Why it matters: Material before M3 (first credited external work) and hard-required before M5 settlements. Also interacts with the GDPR-ledger design (socaity-m2i): DAC7 identity data must live off-ledger.

title: M3 contribution loop: AI-generated PR provenance, license compatibility, DCO/CLA compliance, and defect liability
description: Context: milestones.md M3 — external agent-owners ship PRs into projects their owner does not maintain, targeted via the graph; the platform prices and credits the work. Question: (1) Copyright status and license provenance of agent-generated code contributed under target projects' licenses — who signs the DCO/CLA, and can an agent-owner truthfully certify origin? (2) Does the platform, by pricing/crediting/targeting the contribution, take on any liability for defective or infringing contributions (xz-style supply-chain concerns cut both ways)? (3) What disclosures do consenting OSS projects get about AI provenance — some projects ban AI contributions outright. Why it matters: Material before M3 — the done-when is an external merged PR; a provenance dispute in the first credited PR poisons the trust the milestone exists to create. Platform posture should be marketplace/facilitator, never author of record. Community-builder needs the consent script for target maintainers; agent-engineer needs provenance capture in the loop.

title: M2 observatory: data-source terms, database rights, and publishing funding signals about identifiable maintainers
description: Context: milestones.md M2 ingests npm/PyPI/Maven/GitHub dependency graphs plus funding signals (GitHub Sponsors, Open Collective, OpenSSF) and publishes an index of the most foundational, least-supported software; sustainability.md model 3 sells API access and reports on the same data. Question: (1) Do the APIs and ToS of each source permit ingestion, republication of derived indexes, and commercial resale (reports/API) — GitHub ToS and Sponsors data especially? (2) EU database sui-generis rights on any ingested dataset? (3) Funding signals about individual maintainers (a named person's sponsorship income being visibly low) are personal data — lawful basis, and reputational care in how the index names projects vs people. Why it matters: Material before M2 publication — the index is the press moment (done-when: cited by people we did not contact); a takedown demand or ToS violation at that moment is a launch-killing own-goal. Data-analyst owns source selection, so constraints must reach them before the pipeline is built.

title: Specify the context pack: the per-node artifact agents consume
description: Context: knowledge.md tooling posture: a context pack per graph node (need, acceptance criteria, repo conventions, entry points) is the M3 product surface; the platform provides targets and verification, not a captive runtime. / Question: Specify the context pack format so M1's graph schema already carries its fields — need statement, acceptance criteria, repo conventions pointer, entry points, disclosure/attribution requirements, verification hooks. / Why it matters: If M1 nodes lack acceptance-criteria and convention fields, every node must be re-authored before M3; specifying the pack now costs a page and saves a migration.
close_reason: Implemented doc/context-pack.md with the schema-1 per-node context-pack contract, field semantics, population rules, provenance/consent boundaries, and compatibility guidance. Verified with ./tools/check.sh and green PR #37 checks (reuse, verify, wordlist).

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: [council] Spec constraint from socaity-15b resolution: the context-pack fields ARE the specifiability vector (need statement, acceptance criteria, conventions pointer, verified entry points) — t46's spec should enumerate pack fields as checkable signals so the M2 pipeline pre-builds M3's surface.

title: Consent registry for M3 targets must be designed into M2 outreach
description: Context: knowledge.md quality bar rule 1: consent precedes contribution — only projects that opted in via the M2 index outreach. milestones.md M3 runs on 'a few consenting OSS projects surfaced by the M2 index'. / Question: The M2 observatory outreach must therefore carry an opt-in ask ('may credited agents send issue-first contributions?') and record it somewhere machine-readable. What does the consent record look like (scope, revocation, per-repo policies like AI-PR bans), and who owns the outreach script? / Why it matters: This is an M3 concern requiring an M2-time decision: if outreach happens without the consent ask, we re-contact the same maintainers twice, and one unconsented agent PR wave poisons the well permanently (curl precedent).

title: Deterministic simulation harness: requirements and timing from mechanism-designer
description:
Context: vision.md 'Relationship to ComputeNet' (deterministic simulation for testing mechanisms before deploying) and 'The supply side' (the market is a control system: damping, vesting, stampedes). Charter: simulation is a service to mechanism-designer.
Question: When does mechanism-designer first need strategic-agent simulation (honest/greedy/colluding/Sybil policies), and over which mechanism surface — M3 vesting curves? M4 multiplier damping? Constraint from the platform side: the sim must execute the real mechanism code, not a reimplementation, which requires mechanism code to be deterministic (event-time only, fixed-point arithmetic, no iteration-order dependence) from the first line written.
Why it matters: Not an M0/M1 deliverable, but it imposes a coding discipline on all mechanism code starting at M1; deciding late means the sim lies or the mechanism gets rewritten.

title: Substrate must not assume all state is public: private demand expression and receipt-freeness
description: Context: vision.md 'The demand side' — shape of demand public, identities private; needs are sensitive (health, finance, family). MACI-style receipt-freeness: if a voter can prove how they voted, votes become sellable (vision.md threat model, Sybil demand row). ComputeNet provides 'live, convergent, forkable shared state' (vision.md, Relationship to ComputeNet). / Question: Does the substrate contract admit state that is aggregated-public but individually-private (per-context nullifiers, unlinkable votes, no per-user receipts), or does 'radical transparency + forkable data' currently imply every delta is public? Decide the boundary now: which layers see raw demand events vs only aggregates. / Why it matters: M4 demand democracy is unbuildable on a substrate where every write is publicly attributable — and voters who can prove their vote can sell it. This is a data-model constraint that M1's substrate work is setting today; retrofitting privacy into a convergent replicated log is a rewrite.

title: M1 repo ingestion pulls third-party personal data into needs graphs
description: Context: milestones.md M1 — 'point it at any GitHub repository and it ingests the issue tracker into a needs graph'. Issue trackers contain usernames, emails in commit trailers, and sometimes sensitive personal context from people who never consented to appearing in a socaity graph. M4 later makes graphs multi-player and public. / Question: What are the minimization rules at ingestion (strip author identities? link-not-copy? aggregate-only attribution?), and what is the re-publication boundary when a private single-player graph becomes public? / Why it matters: If M1 graphs silently carry third-party personal data, the M4 flip to public multi-player republishes it — a GDPR problem and a maintainer-trust problem (community-builder's constituency). Cheap to fix at ingestion-schema time, expensive after graphs exist.

title: Estimation semantics at M1: units, intervals, and the calibration gap before M3
description: Context: milestones.md M1 says agents 'estimate nodes'; knowledge.md: agents are systematically overconfident, calibrate against realized effort from merged work — but that data only exists from M3. vision.md: forecasts are intervals, not dates. / Question: What do M1 estimates denominate (agent-hours? tokens? human-review-minutes?), are they intervals from day one, and what is the interim calibration story for the M1-M3 gap (e.g. anchor against historical issue cycle times from the ingested repo itself)? / Why it matters: M1 estimates become the priors that M3+ pricing and forecasting consume; shipping point-estimates in fake units teaches users to distrust the numbers before the market ever exists.

title: M3 consent ladder and agent-PR etiquette specification
description: Context: M3's done-condition is an external agent-owner's PR merged into a project its owner does not maintain (milestones.md M3). knowledge.md consent ladder: project opt-in, maintainer-blessed target issues, etiquette settings (issue-first, disclosure format), visible kill switch; start with 3-5 projects with real relationships. / Question: Turn the ladder into a concrete spec agent-engineer can enforce in the contribution loop: how agents discover a project's etiquette, how disclosure appears in PRs, how the kill switch propagates, and what happens on violation. / Why it matters: Maintainers' current baseline experience of AI PRs is spam; one unsolicited or undisclosed agent PR from the platform destroys the M2-built trust and the M3 done-condition depends on maintainers who feel in control.

title: M2 maintainer outreach playbook: consent before the index names anyone
description: Context: M2 publishes 'the most foundational, least-supported software in the world' (milestones.md M2) — i.e. it names under-supported projects publicly, and it is 'inherently press-worthy'. knowledge.md: personal email to every listed maintainer 2+ weeks ahead, with dossier, correction path, and removal offer. / Question: Formalize the playbook: list size at launch, contact sequencing vs press embargo (launch-strategist), how maintainer corrections feed back into the index (data-analyst), and the removal/opt-out policy. Does press timing pressure ever override the 2-week consent window? (Position: no — needs explicit agreement.) / Why it matters: Being named 'under-supported' must land as advocacy, not exposure; one maintainer experiencing the index as an attack costs more than the press cycle gains, and the OSS world is small and elephant-memoried.

title: Instrument cohort-to-cohort conversion and community health from day one
description: Context: milestones.md (Recruitment chain): each cohort is the supply/demand the next milestone needs; knowledge.md (Metrics): track time-to-first-response, second-contribution rate, cohort-to-cohort conversion, maintainer NPS; ignore stars and member counts. / Question: Define the minimal instrumentation (ledger-derived where possible, privacy-respecting) that measures manifesto-reader -> ledger-contributor -> M1 tool-user conversion, so the M0->M1 transition is observed rather than assumed. / Why it matters: The whole milestone strategy is a conversion chain; without measurement we cannot tell whether an arrow is broken until the next milestone starves.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Metric definitions community-builder can fix now (data-analyst input needed on collection): (1) time-to-first-response on issues/discussions, target < 24h through M1; (2) second-contribution rate — share of external ledger contributors who make a second contribution within 60 days; single best community-health predictor; (3) cohort conversion: unique manifesto readers (site analytics, privacy-respecting) -> ledger contributors -> M1 tool users; (4) maintainer NPS after every M2/M3 contact. Explicitly not tracked as success: stars, member counts, impressions (knowledge.md, Metrics).

title: ledger validator comment overstates: the epoch clamp has two implementations, not one
description: ledger/validator.py's entry_epoch comment says the clamp is recorded 'so replay and the rule agree by construction rather than by two implementations of one rule' — but the clamp is in fact implemented twice, in ledger/validator.py (entry_epoch) and rule/replay.py (epoch_assignment). Drift risk is covered by a single equivalence assertion at rule/test_ledger_integration.py:78. Correct the comment, and consider whether the assertion is enough.
close_reason: Clarified that validator and replay compute epoch assignments independently; documented the full-map integration assertion. Verified with tools/check.sh and 14 rule.test_ledger_integration tests; PR #32 squash-merged.

title: Prepare the public rationale for crypto-ecosystem funding (RetroPGF/Gitcoin) vs the no-token stance
description: Context: knowledge.md: RetroPGF/Gitcoin are philosophically aligned (vision.md cites both as prior art) but brand-sensitive — taking crypto-ecosystem money while holding sustainability.md's hard 'no token issuance' anti-commitment needs a prepared line. Retro rounds reward shipped impact, so relevant from M2, not before. / Question: Draft the one-paragraph public rationale (accepting retro funding for shipped public goods is consistent with rejecting speculative token issuance) and decide whether to enter rounds at all. / Why it matters: an improvised answer under press scrutiny at M2 launch damages the trust asset the anti-commitments exist to build; a prepared one turns the tension into a positioning strength.

title: Track eIDAS 2.0 / EUDI wallet rollout as candidate M4-M5 attestation
description: Context: knowledge.md mechanism landscape — government eID via EUDI wallet is the best EU-native personhood fit (strong Sybil resistance, ZK selective disclosure), but member-state wallet rollout runs 2026+ and pace varies. / Question: By M4 planning time, which member states have production wallets, which attributes are disclosable with ZK/selective disclosure, and does any wallet support the 'distinct human, counted once' predicate without revealing identity? / Why it matters: Long lead time item — if EUDI matures on schedule it collapses the hardest part of M5-grade personhood for EU users; if it slips, M4 needs a stronger non-eID leg. Revisit quarterly; no M0/M1 action beyond keeping credential design compatible.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Snapshot (2026-08, identity-specialist): eIDAS 2.0 in force; member states obligated to offer EUDI wallets, with rollout deadlines landing 2026-2027 and pace varying widely by state. Key open technical question remains whether production wallets expose a ZK/selective-disclosure 'unique natural person' predicate usable as a personhood attestation without identity disclosure — the ARF has been moving toward ZK support but wallet implementations lag the spec. Action: re-check at each milestone boundary; treat EUDI as the STRONG attestation level in the socaity-9p6 menu if the predicate materializes, and plan M4 to function without it.

title: VAT posture across revenue streams (take rate, compute margin, observatory reports, hosting)
description: Context: sustainability.md aligned revenue models 1-4; knowledge layer flags VAT registration as material before M2 (first recurring revenue). Question: Confirm VAT treatment per stream and register at the right moment. Why it matters: First invoices (M2 sponsorships/reports) must be issued correctly; cheap to do right, annoying to amend.

comments.author: MacBoo
comments.text: Resolution (legal-counsel, resolvable alone — analysis for decision-making, not legal advice): (1) Take rate on escrowed fiat rail = platform service fee, VAT-able supply in NL (21%); charge VAT on the fee only, never on the escrowed principal flowing through to contributors. (2) Compute margin = resale of metered services, standard-rated; B2B cross-border EU customers reverse-charged with valid VAT IDs. (3) Observatory sponsorships: genuine donation-like sponsorship without deliverables can fall outside VAT scope, but the moment logo placement/reports/API access are promised it is a standard-rated supply — draft sponsorship agreements accordingly (two templates: donation vs services). (4) Hosted subscriptions = electronically supplied services; B2C cross-border EU sales need OSS (One Stop Shop) registration once over the EUR 10k threshold. Action: register for VAT when the BV is formed (socaity-gp2); until then, small-business scheme (KOR) is possible but usually not worth it if grant/sponsor invoicing is imminent. Engage an NL accountant at first invoice, not before. Closing as resolved on the record.
